A mobile app UI mockup showing a list of redesigned mountain cards for a Summit Tracker app. The background is white/light blue. Show 3 mountain cards stacked vertically:

Card 1 (Summited): A card with rounded corners (12px), subtle shadow. Left side has a beautiful photo-style illustration of Mount Everest with snowy peaks. The photo takes up about 35% of the card width as a rounded square thumbnail. Right side shows: 'Mount Everest' in bold dark navy text (16px), below it 'Nepal · Himalaya' in muted blue-gray, below that '8,849 m / 29,032 ft' in medium weight. A red stamp-style 'SUMMITED' badge overlays the top-right corner of the card at a slight angle, with a small blue date pill 'MAR 15, 2024' beneath it. The card has a very subtle warm tint background.

Card 2 (Not summited): Same layout but with K2 mountain illustration thumbnail. Shows 'K2' bold, 'Pakistan · Karakoram' subtitle, '8,611 m / 28,251 ft'. No summit badge. Clean white background.

Card 3 (Summited): Same layout with Matterhorn illustration thumbnail. Shows 'Matterhorn', 'Switzerland · Alps', '4,478 m / 14,692 ft'. Has the red SUMMITED stamp and blue date pill 'JUN 22, 2023'.

The cards have 12px gaps between them. Each card is about 80px tall. The mountain thumbnails are vivid, atmospheric photos showing the actual mountain silhouettes with sky gradients - not icons. The overall color scheme uses navy (#1A3350), steel blue (#3B6FA0), and white. Modern, clean iOS-style design. Show this on a phone screen frame with the app header 'Summit Tracker' visible at top.

responseMessageContents.text:
Here's my mockup for the redesigned mountain cards:

![Mountain Card Mockup](https://r2-pub.rork.com/generated-images/f193e263-8bf0-4698-b9f9-e06cfbd68951.png)

**The key changes I'd make:**

1. **Photo thumbnails** — Replace the small icon with a rounded square thumbnail showing an atmospheric photo/illustration of each mountain. This gives each card a unique visual identity and makes scrolling the list much more engaging.

2. **Richer layout** — The mountain name, location, and elevation are stacked vertically on the right side of the thumbnail, giving each piece of info room to breathe instead of cramming everything into one row.

3. **Summit badge overlay** — The "SUMMITED" stamp and date pill sit on the card itself (top-right area), making it immediately clear which peaks you've conquered without competing with the mountain info.

4. **Card-based design** — Each mountain gets its own card with rounded corners and subtle shadow, replacing the current flat list-row style. This feels more modern and tappable.

5. **Mountain imagery** — I'd source a unique photo URL for each mountain (from Unsplash or similar) and store those URLs in the mountain data. This is the biggest visual upgrade — real mountain photos make the app feel premium.

Want me to implement this design?
